expectations.text: The output names exactly four options in the Phase 4 respond menu, including 'Reply to agent comment', 'Review the PR', 'Mark unit complete', and 'Done for now' — not six options, no 'Show dependency graph', no 'Dispatch newly unblocked units'.
expectations.evidence:
'1. Reply to agent comment
2. Review the PR  ← you indicated this
3. Mark unit complete
4. Done for now'

expectations.text: When executing the 'Review the PR' branch, the output uses `gh pr view <number>` (or `--json`) and `gh pr diff <number>` to pull PR state.
expectations.evidence: Uses `gh pr view 142 --json ...` but never invokes `gh pr diff 142` to pull the diff.

expectations.text: Any `gh pr list` invocation in the respond loop includes the `--state all` flag (otherwise merged PRs become invisible to the loop).
expectations.evidence: 'gh pr list --state all --search "<issue-number> in:body" ...' and explicit note '--state all is required because gh pr list defaults to open PRs only.'

expectations.text: The output routes review work through the existing `/ce-code-review` skill (via the platform's skill-invocation primitive) OR captures user-typed feedback and posts it via `gh pr review` — it does NOT inline a fresh code-review prompt or invent a new review framework.
expectations.evidence: 'I'd invoke the `ce-code-review` skill via the `Skill` tool' and 'gh pr review 142 --comment --body-file ...'

expectations.text: The output does NOT mention any auto-review / `dispatch_auto_review` config, dependency-aware merge gating, or auto re-dispatch of newly unblocked units.
expectations.evidence: No mention of dispatch_auto_review, auto-review, dependency-aware merge gating, or auto re-dispatch anywhere in the output.

suggestions: Expectation [1] requires both `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff`; consider whether `gh pr diff` is strictly necessary when delegating to `/ce-code-review` (which may fetch its own diff). The conjunction may be overly strict given the skill-routing design.
eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are concrete and well-targeted. The [1]/[3] interaction is slightly in tension: if review is routed to a sub-skill, the orchestrator may legitimately skip fetching the diff itself.
